rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 2 "What your five users did" L18 (expanded view): "your bet, with the signal you agreed; your digest" and chunk 1 L7 "the slice" are spine nouns not named in this file; both are the training's own earned artifacts (apt101-read-the-digest, apt101-write-the-bet exercises precede Day 3). Arc-earned spine carve-out applies. Chunk 1 "That is Jakob Nielsen's rule" binds to the preceding sentence "run small rounds, and many of them". Harm (slide a reader cannot resolve) absent.

Closest: chunk 1 L9 "That is Jakob Nielsen's rule in full (2000)": names a source and unpacks it in the same sentence; no pointer to another file by position. grep for "lecture|earlier file|opening" in body_numbered: none.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 2 L18 "the signal you agreed" and chunk 3 L31 "your bet was written down with its signal before anything was built". Both resolve to beats present: curriculum/exercises/apt101-write-the-bet.md (grep -c "bet" = 26) and apt101-read-the-digest.md (grep -c digest = 18). No "the X you did/saw/caught" with a dead target.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 2 L22 "Which of them would you have found by reading the digest alone?" is a question after the narrated analysis, not a guess-before-reveal demo cue; every sentence is verbed and carries its scene under a muted read. No demo beat in the file.

Closest: chunk 3 L33 "Then the team writes down what it now believes instead, and places the next bet on that." is a short final paragraph, but the slide opens with a self-carrying claim at L29. No slide is a wait-state.

Closest: chunk 2 header L15 "What your five users did, beside what the digest said" vs body: body puts three things side by side (bet+signal, digest, user moments), a label-header that is literally true. Chunk 1 and 3 headers match their bodies (L7-11, L29-33).

Per-chunk read: no "Not X. Not Y. Z." (grep -c "Not .*\. Not " = 0 in body); no anaphora triple (closest chunk 2 L22 "Some moments sharpen it. Some say it was about the wrong step." is a pair); no self-grading superlative ("The best results" L9 is a verbatim Nielsen quote, not a claim about the training); no number+retraction; no abstraction-noun stack; no verb triplet with empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 1 L9 "small rounds" and chunk 3 L31 "pivot or persevere" are ordinary product vocabulary. grep for surface-as-noun|compendium|forcing function|firing|mood|beat in body_numbered: 0 hits (view has no body hits). "slice", "digest", "signal" are training-taught terms, audience-facing.

rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c "\*\*" over the three slide-file bodies above their maintainer tails: 0 bold spans in the expanded body (L1-34).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.

No phase-less prose section.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 1 L4 "Test with five users, fix, then test five more" is imperative in a lecture; chunk 2 L15 is a catalogue label naming its subject (NOT a violation per the rule); chunk 3 L26 "A slice that comes back no has done its job" is a claim. Headers are squint titles by maintainer STATUS note; the rule fires non-blocking only on law/consolidation slides, and chunk 1 teaches a method instruction, so the mood-switch harm (a declarative heading failing to land inside an exercise) is absent in a lecture.
